Article Title: Rupee falls 10 paise to 94.66 against US dollar as crude nears $98
Article Text:
Rupee falls 10 paise to 94.66 against US dollar as crude nears $98

Rupee remained under pressure in early trade on Tuesday, slipping 10 paise to 94.66 against the US dollar as rising crude prices and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East weighed on investor sentiment.The currency had opened at 94.49 against the dollar at the interbank foreign exchange market before moving down to 94.66. This followed a 13-paise decline on Monday, when rupee settled at 94.56.The pressure on the currency came as Brent crude climbed towards $97 a barrel. Brent, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.63 per cent higher at $97.61 per barrel in futures trade amid escalating US-Iran tensions and concerns over possible disruption to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.Despite these pressures, forex traders said rupee continued to remain range-bound, helped by RBI dollar sales and strong foreign-currency inflows under special schemes."The RBI's intervention has been particularly important in preventing higher oil prices from translating into a weaker rupee," Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director, Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP, said.Bhansali expects rupee to trade between 94.00 and 94.75. He said crude was near the $97 level, while the dollar index had fallen to 98.74 and the RBI continued to sell dollars, keeping the rupee within the range.Markets are now awaiting US and India CPI data and the FOMC meeting on September 16 for further cues, Bhansali said.The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, was at 98.80, down 0.37 per cent.Domestic equities also opened lower with Sensex falling 382.25 points to 75,750.56, while the Nifty declined 97.80 points to 23,681.80. Foreign institutional investors were net buyers in the previous session, purchasing equities worth Rs 280.13 crore on Monday, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee falls 10 paise to 94.66 against US dollar as crude nears $98 a barrel. This followed a 13-paise decline on Monday, when rupee settled at 94.56. Domestic equities also opened lower with Sensex falling 382.25 points.

Article Title: Iran doubles petrol price for heavy users as currency touches record low
Article Text:
Iran doubles petrol prices

Currency hits record lows

Iran has doubled the price of petrol for consumers who exceed their monthly quota, putting a higher cost on heavy fuel use as households already grapple with falling purchasing power and soaring inflation.The revised rate came into effect early Tuesday and applies to purchases above 110 litres (29 gallons) a month. Consumers crossing that limit will now pay 100,000 rials (about 7 cents) per litre, compared with the rate introduced in December.The government said the additional money generated from the increase would be distributed to households. Its announcement referred to the “current situation” without specifically mentioning the war with the United States.This is the second increase in petrol prices since December. Such increases have historically been politically sensitive in Iran, with a price rise in 2019 triggering nationwide protests followed by a crackdown that reportedly killed more than 300 people.The latest increase comes at a time when the Iranian currency has been weakening sharply and people's purchasing power has declined. The US dollar was trading at 2.22 million rials on Monday.Iran nevertheless continues to have some of the world's lowest petrol prices. But the higher rate for heavy users adds another pressure point for a population of more than 90 million.Keramat Veis Karami, CEO of the state oil distribution company, said that the new rate would apply to 15 per cent of consumers, according to the official IRNA news agency.The change also comes against the backdrop of record fuel consumption. Karami said Iran consumed 145 million litres (38 million gallons) of petrol per day in August, compared with domestic production capacity of 122 million litres per day. The balance is imported.The higher price is intended to help bring down consumption, which experts have linked to ageing cars and spare parts in Iran, along with insufficient public transportation.But petrol prices are closely tied to the wider cost of living. Experts have warned that higher fuel prices will add to inflation in a country already facing an annual inflation rate of about 67 per cent, according to the country's statistics centre, a government agency.The sensitivity around petrol prices is not new. Cheap gasoline has for generations been viewed as a birthright in Iran. A price increase in 1964 triggered mass demonstrations and led the shah to deploy military vehicles to replace those of striking taxi drivers.
Article Summary: The revised rate came into effect early Tuesday and applies to purchases above 110 litres (29 gallons) a month. Consumers crossing that limit will now pay 100,000 rials (about 7 cents) per litre. The government said the additional money generated from the increase would be distributed to households.

Article Title: Brent crude climbs beyond $97 as Strait of Hormuz disruptions choke global oil supplies
Article Text:
Brent crude climbs beyond $97 as Strait of Hormuz disruptions choke global oil supplies

Trump claims oil prices

Iran warns of retaliation

Oil prices inched higher on Tuesday as conflict in the Middle East continues to intensify, disrupting global oil supplies for over six months now. Brent crude was up 0.05%, or $0.05, at $97.05 while WTI crude rose 1.03%, or $0.94, to $92.42.The latest gains came after Iran warned that it would retaliate against any further US attacks on its assets, adding to concerns that the conflict could drag on and threaten energy infrastructure and shipping in the Gulf.The Strait of Hormuz remains a focus for traders, with heightened tensions around the key route for global crude shipments prompting them to build a risk premium into oil prices. Brent had already climbed to its highest level since July 24 in the previous session.Iran on Monday warned that energy infrastructure across the Gulf, including US oil and gas interests, was vulnerable. The warning followed a weekend of tit-for-tat strikes, with no indication of progress towards a diplomatic breakthrough.The US strikes on Saturday targeted three Iranian oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub, according to US Central Command. The attacks came after strikes by Iran's Revolutionary Guards on US warships operating in the region.The escalation has also prompted Goldman Sachs to revise its oil-price outlook. The bank raised its Brent and WTI forecasts by $5 to $85 and $80, respectively, for December 2026. For 2027, it raised its forecasts to $80 and $75, respectively, based on a new assumption that disruptions to Middle East shipping will continue into 2027.Marex analyst Ed Meir also expects crude prices to remain elevated through the end of the year as long as the war continues. In the financial services platform's September commodity outlook, Meir said this was likely given "the multitude of issues that have yet to be addressed".US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, said oil prices would fall sharply once the US achieves victory in its conflict with Iran and predicted that gas prices could eventually fall below two dollars per gallon.In a post on his Truth Social platform, Trump directly linked high energy costs to the ongoing military operations in the Middle East and said markets would stabilise rapidly after the conflict."Oil prices will drop precipitously, like everything else is dropping (but more!), when we WIN the war with Iran," Trump wrote. "Three Dollars a gallon, but ultimately, below Two Dollars a gallon."Trump also repeated his warning that the US would not allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon."It will all happen quickly, and Iran will never have a Nuclear Weapon. MAGA!" he added.Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf had earlier warned Washington against any misadventures towards Iranian energy facilities, saying there would be sharp repercussions.In a post on X, Ghalibaf said Iran's oil and gas production chain is "sprawling, accessible, and exposed."He added, "American oil and gas companies across these waters and facilities share that exposure. Strike our assets, and you get struck. We’ve already proven it. Ask the bases that are no longer viable."Alongside the post, Ghalibaf shared an image stating, "The lost decade of the US Economy is coming, because some clowns at DOW decided so."His comments came as he shared a post by US secretary of war Pete Hegseth, who claimed that Iran's "oil tanker fleet is defenceless" and reiterated Washington's claims that Iran's navy and air force had been destroyed.
Article Summary: Brent crude was up 0.05%, or $0.05, at $97.05 while WTI crude rose 1.03%, or £0.94, to $92.42. The latest gains came after Iran warned that it would retaliate against any further US attacks on its assets.

Article Title: Woman returned from maternity leave to the same Rs 2.6 lakh monthly salary but fewer managerial duties; Delhi HC awards Rs 10 lakh, says pay alone cannot protect career
Article Text:
The High Court has made it clear that the statutory safeguard also covers the work she performs. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

What the company said

Creche availability

Why Delhi High Court ruled in favour of the woman

A woman with 14 years’ experience returned to her job after maternity leave only to find that while her salary had remained the same, her managerial duties had been reduced. Now the Delhi High Court has ruled that maternity protection cannot be treated as a matter of simply preserving a woman employee's salary and job title.The High Court has made it clear that the statutory safeguard also covers the work she performs, her position in the organisational hierarchy, supervisory powers and opportunities for appraisal and promotion.Justice Sachin Datta, in a judgment delivered on August 31, 2026, said a woman who returns to work after maternity leave should ordinarily be placed back in the post she occupied before going on leave.If that position has ceased to exist for genuine and demonstrable organisational reasons, the employer must provide another role that is as close as reasonably possible to the original one in terms of pay, grade, status, responsibilities, managerial authority and opportunities for career progression.The ruling came on a petition filed by Chartered Accountant Rakhi Bisht, who claimed that her professional position was adversely affected after she informed her employer about her pregnancy and subsequently returned from maternity leave.Bisht had about 14 years of professional experience when she joined the organisation in 2022 as Manager, Accounting, drawing a monthly salary of Rs 2.60 lakh, according to an ANI report.As per her case, she informed the management about her pregnancy in May 2023 and was later moved to another team. She went on maternity leave in December 2023 and returned to work in July 2024.After resuming duty, she was informed that her previous position was no longer available and was instead placed in the Treasury Department. Bisht alleged that the new assignment was substantially inferior to the managerial accounting responsibilities she had earlier handled. She also claimed that she was given no reporting staff and was kept out of managerial meetings.The employer denied Bisht's allegations, saying there had been no change in her designation, level, salary or seniority.It maintained that, following an organisational restructuring, she was given investment accounting and currency revaluation responsibilities while continuing at the same managerial level.The issue of the creche facility at the workplace was also considered by the High Court.Bisht had approached the employer about the availability of a creche in September 2024. She was initially told that no such facility was available at that time. The employer subsequently took the position that a creche did exist, but was not functional on the days relevant to her request.The High Court held that merely having a creche facility is not enough if it cannot actually be used when an employee requires it. A facility that is non-functional at the relevant time does not meet the statutory requirement under Section 11-A of the Maternity Benefit Act.The Court said an employer cannot comply with the law on paper by retaining a woman's salary and designation while taking away meaningful responsibilities, decision-making authority or future career opportunities. Doing so, it observed, would effectively permit the employer to accomplish indirectly something that cannot be done directly under the law.The High Court also clarified the scope of Section 12(1) of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961. The provision bars an employer from changing the conditions of a woman's service to her disadvantage during the period of her statutorily protected absence. According to the Court, this protection is not limited to cases where employment itself is terminated.The phrase "conditions of service", it said, encompasses the substantive elements of a person's employment. This includes the nature and substance of the duties assigned, grade and functional position, reporting structure, supervisory responsibilities, as well as the employee's consideration for appraisal and promotion."Retention of the same designation and remuneration is, therefore, necessary but not by itself sufficient" where other aspects of employment are changed to the employee's detriment, the Court held.Such an interpretation would turn Section 12 into little more than a formality and undermine the purpose of maternity legislation, the Court said. The legislation is intended to safeguard the dignity of motherhood, economic security and a woman's professional standing.The Court found inconsistencies in the employer's own pleadings and communications. It noted that the employer had said Bisht's earlier position had been assigned to another employee who was promoted while she was away on maternity leave. An internal communication placed before the Court also referred to assigning activities to Bisht merely to "keep her engaged" after her return.The Court ordered respondent no. 2 to pay Bisht compensation of Rs 10 lakh, besides Rs 1.5 lakh towards costs. While determining the compensation, it took into account her professional standing as a Chartered Accountant, her approximately 14 years of experience and her monthly salary of Rs 2.6 lakh. The compensation, the Court noted, was roughly equal to four months' salary.The compensation and costs have to be paid within eight weeks. If the payment is not made within that period, the amount will attract interest at 9% per annum from the date of the judgment until it is realised.The Court therefore held that, as a general rule, a woman returning from maternity leave is entitled to be restored to the position she held before her leave.If that position has genuinely become unavailable because of demonstrable organisational reasons, the employer must offer an alternative that is substantially equivalent. The comparison cannot be limited to salary alone and must also take into account grade, status, role, responsibilities, managerial authority and prospects for career advancement.The employer is also required to explain to the woman, before she returns to work, why her previous position is no longer available. It must also spell out the details of the role being offered in its place, including the grade, remuneration, reporting structure and duties attached to it.If the employee raises an objection to the proposed arrangement, the employer has to consider it and convey its decision in writing, along with reasons for that decision.The Court also made it clear that a woman can herself request changes to her duties, working hours, workplace, work pattern or even seek an alternative role after returning from maternity leave.However, such a request cannot subsequently be treated as her acceptance of reduced service conditions or as a waiver of the statutory protection available to her. Nor can the arrangement be held against her when her appraisal, increment or promotion is considered.The employer had challenged the maintainability of the petition under Article 226, arguing that the matter arose from a private employment relationship and concerned contractual conditions of service.The High Court did not accept this contention. It held that Bisht was not asking the Court to enforce a contractual provision, but was seeking protection available to her under Section 12 of the Maternity Benefit Act.The Court also referred to Section 27 of the Act, which gives its provisions an overriding effect over any inconsistent terms contained in an employment contract. On that basis, it held that an employer cannot avoid a statutory obligation simply because it is a private entity.The High Court further turned down the argument that Bisht had an alternative statutory remedy. It said the case raised questions involving fundamental rights and constitutional issues relating to equality, dignity and maternity protection. The Court also noted that the relevant rules and schemes under the Code on Social Security, 2020 had not yet been framed.The High Court also issued broader directions concerning maternity safeguards that could affect private employers. It directed the Union of India to use its powers under Sections 149, 150 and 154 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 to frame rules or schemes, or issue directions, aimed at ensuring effective implementation of maternity protections.The proposed framework is to address several areas, including workplace accommodation related to pregnancy, protection of an employee's role and status after maternity leave, lactation support, disclosure and functioning of creche facilities, timelines for dealing with maternity-related grievances, safeguards against retaliation and the designation of authorities empowered to receive and decide complaints, including requests for urgent interim protection. The exercise is to be completed within six months from the date of the judgment.The framework contemplated by the Court would also require pregnancy-related accommodation requests to be assessed in writing. It would provide safeguards against compelling an employee to take leave or accept an inferior position, require reasoned written decisions where an employee's role or reporting structure is affected, and protect employees from retaliation.In its concluding observations, the Court said the constitutional protections under Articles 14, 15, 21 and 42, read together with maternity legislation, mean that pregnancy and motherhood cannot be allowed to result in professional disadvantage.The petition filed by Bisht was accordingly disposed of with the declarations, compensation and directions set out above.
Article Summary: Rakhi Bisht had about 14 years of professional experience when she joined the organisation in 2022 as Manager, Accounting. She informed the management about her pregnancy in May 2023 and was later moved to another team. She went on maternity leave and returned to work in July 2024. After resuming duty, she was informed that her previous position was no longer available and was instead placed in the Treasury Department.

Article Title: Rs 20,700 crore, 326 km more: India completes its Dedicated Freight Corridor network as PM Modi inaugurates three new sections; now fully operational across 2,843 km with 443 trains daily as of now
Article Text:
Together, these stretches cover 326 route kilometres and have been developed at a cost of more than Rs 20,700 crore.

Dedicated Freight Corridor Network Complete

Dedicated Freight Corridors

Year Freight loading (in Million Tonnes) 2014-15 1098 2015-16 1104 2016-17 1109 2017-18 1162 2018-19 1223 2019-20 1210 2020-21 1233 2021-22 1418 2022-23 1512 2023-24 1591 2024-25 1617 2025-26 1670

Some of the major initiatives include:

Terminal Development:

Wagon Investment Schemes:

Joint Parcel Product-Rapid Cargo Service (JPP-RCS) scheme:

CONCOR:

India’s dedicated freight corridors network is expanding with Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurating some key new sections on Tuesday. PM Modi dedicated three key sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) to the nation. Together, these stretches cover 326 route kilometres and have been developed at a cost of more than Rs 20,700 crore. The sections are New Sanand (N)-New Makarpura, New Umbergaon-New Saphale and New Saphale-New JNPT.The Ministry of Railways undertook the construction of two Dedicated Freight Corridors. The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) runs from Ludhiana to Sonnagar and covers 1,337 km, while the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) connects Dadri with Jawaharlal Nehru Port Terminal (JNPT) over 1,506 km.The direct link to the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) is expected to speed up the movement of EXIM cargo, improve connectivity between industrial hubs and ports, bring down logistics costs and ease congestion on Mumbai's railway network.With these sections commissioned, the entire Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) network has become operational across its full length. The dedicated freight infrastructure is also expected to strengthen India's logistics network by improving multimodal connectivity, cutting transit times and allowing cargo to move more seamlessly between different regions.PM Modi also flagged off freight train services from New Sanand (North), New Makarpura, New Umbergaon and New JNPT in Mumbai.Till the commissioning, it was reported that the two corridors together handle an average of around 443 trains every day. Their operational performance has remained strong, with freight volumes rising steadily alongside higher average speeds, quicker turnaround times and improved reliability, according to the Ministry of Railways.The DFC network has also freed up additional capacity on the conventional railway network by shifting freight traffic to the EDFC and WDFC. This has allowed the Railways to operate more goods and coaching services across its network.According to Indian Railways, the Dedicated Freight Corridor project is having a positive impact on transportation and logistics. This is due to greater movement of Double Stack Container (DSC) trains and higher axle load trains. DFCs also provide faster access from the northern hinterland to Western portsUnion Budget 2026 announced a new Dedicated Freight Corridor linking Dankuni in the east with Surat in the west. The work on preparing or updating the Detailed Project Report for the proposed corridor has already started.The Ministry of Railways said that these initiatives have contributed to an increase in freight loading and revenue for the national transporter over the past few years.Indian Railways' freight loading rose to 1,670 MT in 2025-26, making it the second-largest freight-carrying railway system in the world.Indian Railways has also adopted a multi-pronged approach to strengthen freight logistics, improve regional connectivity and raise the Railways' share in freight transportation. The strategy focuses on making freight operations more efficient, improving connectivity between regions and creating stronger first-and-last-mile logistics solutions.Indian Railways is taking a two-pronged approach to improve freight handling at terminals. This includes promoting modern rail freight terminals under the Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal (GCT) policy, while also upgrading and expanding infrastructure at goods sheds owned by the Railways.Indian Railways has introduced several schemes to facilitate private sector investment in wagons. These include specialised wagons designed for particular commodities such as cement, oil, steel and fly-ash.The JPP-RCS scheme is designed to provide customised logistics solutions based on the specific requirements of customers, including door-to-door parcel services.It also provides for online booking of parcel space through aggregators, in addition to India Post, using the ‘Virtual Aggregation Platform (VAP)’.CONCOR, a PSU under the Ministry of Railways, is using the JPP-RCS to provide door-to-door parcel services on the Delhi-Kolkata and Mumbai-Kolkata sectors.CONCOR is also operating a pilot project at Sonik Goods Shed to provide door-to-door logistics services.
Article Summary: PM Modi dedicated three key sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) to the nation. Together, these stretches cover 326 route kilometres and have been developed at a cost of more than Rs 20,700 crore. The sections are New Sanand (N), New Makarpura, New Umbergaon and New Saphale. The direct link to the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority is expected to speed up the movement of EXIM cargo.

Article Title: Gold price prediction today: Will gold prices continue to drop? Check September 8, 2026 outlook
Article Text:
Gold is expected to range trade in the run up to the US inflation data.

Gold price prediction

today:

Gold prices are expected to remain range-bound for the coming days, says Praveen Singh, Head Currencies and Commodities, Mirae Asset ShareKhan.

Gold Performance:

On September 7, spot gold traded with a slightly bearish tilt as rise in oil prices and strong US nonfarm payroll report released on September 4 outweighed the impact of a retreat in the US Dollar Index.

Earlier, in the week ending September 4, spot gold closed with a weekly loss of nearly 0.55% at $4430 as traders priced in an increased probability of a rate hike on encouraging monthly US job reports.

At the time of writing this article on the night of September 7, the yellow metal was trading with a daily loss of ~0.35% at $4414.

Data roundup:

No US data were released on September 7 as the US observed a Labour Day Holiday.

In its final reading, the Eurozone's 2Q GDP grew 0.6% QoQ, vs the estimate of 0.4%, as Ireland's economic output surged.

US nonfarm payroll report for August released on September 4, turned out to be a solid report as US employers added 162K jobs, Vs the forecast of 55K, while prior month's data was revised higher from -23K in July to 21K. Three-month average job additions were revised higher from 38K to 71K. Manufacturing jobs increased by 16K, Vs the estimate of 5K. The unemployment rate was steady at 4.1%. Labour force participation rate edged higher from 61.5% in July to 61.6%-- first improvement in almost a year. Average weekly hours all employees increased from 34.30 to 34.4, adding millions of productive hours, which can support consumer spending. On the flip side, average hourly earnings rose 0.3% from July and 3.1% from a year earlier, the slowest since 2021. The underemployment rate fell to 7.7% -- the lowest since June 2025.

Gold slumped in the wake of the nonfarm payroll report; however, it cut its losses as the US President Trump, through a social media post, nudged the Fed Chair Warsh cut rates. He also threatened to cut trade ties with nations running trade surplus with the US if the Fed does not lower rates.

US ISM services rose from 54.1 in July to 55.40 in August - quickest since February. The trade deficit surged from $71.20 billion in June to $90.20 billion in July (forecast -$90.2 billion). ISM manufacturing expanded for the eighth straight month, while trade balance in August recorded the largest deficit since March 2025.

Geopolitics and oil:

Crude oil prices rose Monday as traders assessed the risk to supply due to US-Iran conflict. The two countries exchanged tanker strikes over the weekend, which supported oil prices.

On September 7, Iran said the Hormuz deal with Oman is imminent. The agreement, which Iran and Oman have been negotiating for weeks, will include details on a temporary safe route through the crucial transit point for energy supplies, according to Ismail Baghaei, the spokesperson for Iran's Foreign Ministry.

Iran and Oman intend to formalize control of the Strait, and are likely to impose service fees, which may create friction with the US.

The US, blockading Iranian ports to prevent oil exports from Iran, wants the waterway to revert to its pre-war status of being free to use.

The US admitted that a nuclear deal with Iran may never happen.

At the time of writing this article, near-month Brent oil futures were trading with an intra-day gain of 1% at $97.21.

Dated Brent oil closed at $100.65 on September 4.

ETF and COMEX inventory:

Total known global gold ETF holdings fell for the first time in four days on September 4. Holdings have surged quite sharply from the cycle low of 96.16 Moz observed on July 20. To put it in perspective, since that cycle low, net inflows have risen 102 tons. Consequently, ETF holdings are up 0.49 Moz YTD, which amounts to a net inflow of 15.10 tons this year, though, overall, the level is still down 46 tons from the cycle peak seen just before the start of the Iran war on February 28.

Registered COMEX inventories at 15.11 Moz are up 6.4% from the cycle low noted on August 7 but are down ~38% from the record peak of 24.25 Moz seen in April 2025.

China extends its gold buying spree:

China added the most gold to its reserves since 2023 in August, as its official gold holdings rose by 650,000 ounces (~21 tons). The purchase has extended the PBOC’s buying streak to 22 months.

Dollar Index and yields:

Article Title: Alternate fuels overtake petrol in passenger car sales
Article Text:
CNG biggest alternative to petrol

CNG biggest alternative to petrol

NEW DELHI: India’s passenger vehicle market appears to be moving beyond the phase where alternative powertrains were a niche choice. In Aug, CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles together overtook petrol-powered cars for the first time, pointing to a broader change in how buyers are weighing fuel costs, technology and long-term ownership.Alternative fuels accounted for 41.9% of passenger vehicle retail sales, edging past petrol at 40.8%, according to FADA. CNG was the biggest contributor with a 25.2% share, followed by hybrids at 9% and EVs at 7.6%. A year ago, petrol had led the alternative-fuel basket by nearly 11 percentage points. Diesel cars, meanwhile, accounted for 17.2% share of retail sales.The crossover is significant because it is not being driven by a single technology. CNG has become the biggest alternative to petrol on the back of lower running costs, hybrids are finding more takers among buyers seeking better efficiency without depending on charging infrastructure, while EVs continue to expand their footprint.FADA said running-cost economics and continuing hesitation around the E20 transition were nudging buyers towards CNG, hybrids and EVs. Petrol, however, remains the single-largest individual fuel type.Among manufacturers, Maruti Suzuki dominated the CNG segment with around 71% share, while Tata Motors led electric passenger vehicles with around 43% share.The shift is also visible beyond cars. In two-wheelers, EV penetration rose to 10.7% in Aug from 7.7% a year ago, crossing the 10% mark in a non-festive month for the first time. That suggests electric scooters are increasingly moving beyond early adoption and becoming part of the mainstream commuter market.Three-wheelers are already much further along that transition. EVs accounted for 65.3% of sales in Aug, up from 56.6% a year earlier, making the category structurally electric. Commercial vehicles are starting from a much smaller base, but EV share more than doubled to an all-time high of 5.2% from 2.1%, indicating that electrification is beginning to move beyond pilots into fleet purchases.Across all vehicle categories, EV retail sales reached 2.98 lakh units in Aug, up 52.9% year-on-year. The broader signal is that India’s mobility transition is no longer centred only on EVs; consumers are increasingly choosing from a wider mix of alternatives to petrol depending on use case, price and infrastructure.
Article Summary: India’s passenger vehicle market appears to be moving beyond the phase where alternative powertrains were a niche choice. In Aug, CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles together overtook petrol-powered cars for the first time. Diesel cars, meanwhile, accounted for 17.2% share of retail sales.

Article Title: India joins US, 24 nations in push for next-generation 6G networks
Article Text:
Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada met US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the sidelines of the G20 Summit

NEW DELHI: India has joined the United States and 24 other countries in an initiative aimed at shaping the development of next-generation 6G networks, the US department of commerce said.Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada met US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial, where the two discussed the future of 6G technology.“Today, we are pleased to announce that India has joined the US and 24 other countries in the effort to ensure that next-generation networks reflect our shared security interests, strengthen our competitiveness, and drive innovation in 6G,” the department said in a post on X.This comes as Miami in the US hosts the G20 Summit, where Union minister of state for commerce Jitin Prasada attended the ministerial meet.

Article Title: Swiggy swaps retail platform Lynk for 3.2% Udaan stake
Article Text: MUMBAI: Swiggy is selling its retail distribution platform Lynk Logistics to B2B e-commerce startup Udaan, the companies said on Monday. As part of the deal, which has been structured as a share-swap transaction, Swiggy will acquire a 2.8% stake in Udaan.The food and grocery delivery major will also make a cash infusion of Rs 75 crore in the company, buying an additional 0.4% stake, taking its total shareholding in Udaan to 3.2%. The deal will value Lynk at Rs 500 crore.The development comes less than two months after Udaan struck a $160 million financing deal with existing and new investors, averting bankruptcy. Global creditors of the company had initiated insolvency proceedings against Udaan's Singapore-based parent over a $170 million bond default. The startup, which plans to go public, claimed that the recapitalisation has boosted its balance sheet and it has achieved EBITDA profitability in its largest operating city, Bengaluru."Bringing Lynk together with Udaan combines complementary capabilities with Udaan's scale and technology-led platform serving India's retail ecosystem," said Rahul Bothra, CFO at Swiggy.Founded in 2015, Lynk was acquired by Swiggy through a share swap deal with Chennai-based Ramco Group in 2023.Udaan said the acquisition will strengthen its distribution platform and allow the firm to connect consumer brands with a wider network of retailers. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Kolkata collectively contribute nearly 75% of Lynk's revenues, giving Udaan deeper access to key markets.
Article Summary: Swiggy is selling its retail distribution platform Lynk Logistics to B2B e-commerce startup Udaan. As part of the deal, which has been structured as a share-swap transaction, Swiggy will acquire a 2.8% stake. The food and grocery delivery major will also make a cash infusion of Rs 75 crore in the company.

Article Title: SBM India to divest up to 26% equity
Article Text: NEW DELHI: SBM India, a subsidiary of State Bank of Mauritius, is looking to divest up to 26% of its equity in coming months, ED & CFO Amit Jagdhari told TOI on Monday."We have approved in-principle the divestment plan. The process has just started and we have appointed EY as our investment banker. We are open to both private equity or family-owned capital. We have received some preliminary bids, though a timeline can't be framed at this point, as we have to seek approvals from regulators as well," said Jagdhari.The amount of capital to be raised, which has not yet been finalised, will be used "purely" for expansion."The Mauritius parent is also very keen to grow the India footprint," Jagdhari further added.The bank, which received universal banking licence from RBI in 2018, currently has 23 branches and manages assets of Rs 11,450 crore and is set to receive the second tranche of Rs 75 crore from its parent in Mauritius by Sept-end.
Article Summary: SBM India, a subsidiary of State Bank of Mauritius, is looking to divest up to 26% of its equity in coming months. The amount of capital to be raised, which has not yet been finalised, will be used "purely" for expansion.

Article Title: Amid cost-saving drive, JLR to cut 4k jobs over 2 years
Article Text:
Amid cost-saving drive, JLR to cut 4k jobs over 2 years

MUMBAI: Jaguar Land Rover will cut about 4,000 jobs - just under 10% of its 43,000-strong global workforce - over the next two years, as part of a transformation plan aimed at countering US tariff pressures and intensifying competition from carmakers based in China.The Tata Motors-owned group said in a statement it is targeting £1.7 billion ($2.3 billion) in savings over two years to push its break-even point towards 300,000 units. The cuts will not touch direct manufacturing roles and will be achieved through voluntary means wherever possible. Most job losses will fall in the UK, where JLR is based.The UK govt will not intervene to prevent the restructuring, British media has reported. JLR said the savings would strengthen its ability to deliver profitable growth.The company's troubles have mounted. Revenue fell nearly 10% in its most recent quarter, and pretax profit dropped 69% to £109 million. A cyber-attack last year forced JLR to halt production for more than a month, compounding losses already strained by Trump's tariffs.To blunt the tariff impact, JLR plans to build new Defender-branded vehicles inside existing Stellantis plants in the US - a move that lets it assemble vehicles on American soil without the capital outlay of a standalone factory.JLR said in the statement that the restructuring would cut organisational complexity and support its commitment to invest £15-18 billion in electrification, digital technology, advanced manufacturing and customer experience over the next five years.
Article Summary: The Tata Motors-owned group said in a statement it is targeting £1.7 billion ($2.3 billion) in savings over two years. The cuts will not touch direct manufacturing roles and will be achieved through voluntary means wherever possible. JLR said the savings would strengthen its ability to deliver profitable growth.

Article Title: We'll make Air India great again: Gebremariam
Article Text:
We'll make Air India great again: Gebremariam

To Focus On Safety, Operational Execution, Customer Trust & Cost Discipline: Chandra

NEW DELHI: "Focus on safety, financial stability, winning trust of passengers and offer a consistent customer experience." Tata Sons and Air India chairman N Chandrasekaran Monday set the objectives for the airline and its new boss in a town hall with the carrier's outgoing and incoming MDs and CEOs Campbell Wilson and Tewolde Gebremariam, respectively. Taking a leaf from Trump's MAGA, Gebremariam promised to "make Air India great again" as the airline tries to come out of some serious turbulence.Chandra acknowledged that the last 18 months had been particularly challenging for the airline due to geopolitical disruptions, airspace closures, fuel volatility and the deadly Ahmedabad crash. "For me, bringing Air India back to the Tata Group is one of the most important milestones of my career... AI belongs to a billion people.... It is probably the only business that a billion people talk about, have views on, criticise fiercely and appreciate at times. ... all these one billion people are rooting for AI. That is our biggest strength," said Chandra, who has announced he is not going to seek a fresh term as Tata boss next Feb.The "next phase" of AI will focus on safety, customer trust, operational execution and cost discipline."The most important thing Air India should aspire to have is trust in the minds of people. AI must be known for caring about safety above everything else. Our safety record should not just match the best airlines in the world, it should be better than the best," he said.Given AI's mounting losses in a tough operating environment and a bloated cost structure, Chandra urged employees to help build a stronger culture of cost consciousness so that the airline becomes financially sustainable. "Every individual in Air India can contribute to improving cost efficiency."Gebremariam, who is credited with turning around Ethiopian Airlines group during his long stint there, will take over as AI MD and CEO after getting the required security clearance. Setting his priorities, he has set sight on fixing the basics first with safety at the top. "A safety-first culture has to be our number one priority. It is not enough to say it. We must live it every day. If something is not right, stop. Every employee should feel empowered to raise concerns, and I will support that culture. ""Operational excellence is about getting the basics right every day: On-time departures, on-time arrivals, baggage delivery and clean aircraft. Customer experience is a function of operational excellence. We need to minimise disruptions and when they do occur, handle them professionally and take care of our customers," Gebremariam said. Seeking employees' support in turning around AI, he said: "We cannot bring about meaningful change without the commitment of our people. Together, we can build a safer, stronger and truly world class AI."Noting the progress made in last four years, outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson said: "I would like to acknowledge all Air Indians whose commitment, resilience and hard work have made this transformation possible. As the chairman said, this is a task that is not yet complete. The transformation will continue, and Air India's best days are still ahead."
Article Summary: Chandra acknowledged that the last 18 months had been particularly challenging for the airline due to geopolitical disruptions, airspace closures, fuel volatility and the deadly Ahmedabad crash. Gebremariam promised to "make Air India great again" as the airline tries to come out of some serious turbulence.

Article Title: 6-week high: India's crude import price hits $100-a-barrel mark
Article Text:
Crude import price hits $100-a-barrel mark

Likely To Rise Further Amid West Asia Crisis

NEW DELHI: India's average crude import price crossed the $100 per barrel mark for the first time in six weeks last Friday and is likely to rise further as international crude prices surge amid intensified hostilities in West Asia and supply disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz.Indian basket of crude oil - derived average of the sweet-grade global benchmark Dated Brent and the sour-grade benchmarks of Oman and Dubai - increased to $101.07 per barrel Friday, the highest since July 23, Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell data showed.Along with crude, international free-on-board (FOB) prices of petrol and diesel have also surged. While the international FOB price of diesel has averaged $156.88 a barrel this month, up from $149.35 in Aug, the corresponding price for petrol has averaged $122.12 this month, compared to $110.87 in Aug. Premium on diesel over crude has narrowed to 55% from 70% in the last 10 days. The crude basket has so far averaged $99.38 per barrel in Sept, up from $90.19 in Aug. It was above $100 per barrel during the peak of the conflict in March, April and May.An oil company executive said this could lead to higher under-recoveries for oil marketing companies (OMCs) if prices remain elevated for a longer duration and retail pump prices remain unchanged.Oil retailers were making an under-recovery of more than Rs 1,000 crore a day during the peak of the conflict in May, when the Indian basket of crude oil averaged more than $110 per barrel.Ratings agency ICRA said renewed hostilities between Iran and the US pose a challenge for the limited crude oil supplies coming through the Strait of Hormuz. "As Iran threatens to establish a new restricted maritime zone extending beyond the Strait of Hormuz, additional energy flows beyond the latter could be at risk. Owing to these developments, crude oil prices have increased in the past few days, and the Indian crude basket has crossed the $100/barrel mark," said Prashant Vasisht, senior vice-president and co-group head, corporate ratings, ICRA.
Article Summary: Indian basket of crude oil increased to $101.07 per barrel Friday, the highest since July 23. International free-on-board (FOB) prices of petrol and diesel have also surged. Premium on diesel over crude has narrowed to 55% from 70% in the last 10 days.

Article Title: Carbon pricing relief for Indian exporters to UK
Article Text:
The UK Treasury has agreed to recognise India's carbon credit trading scheme, potentially allowing exporters to avoid paying carbon charges twice.

NEW DELHI: In a boost for businesses, the UK has agreed to recognize India’s carbon credit trading scheme, which will enable exporters to avoid “double taxation".Officials said that the UK treasury has agreed to govt’s argument and decided to exempt goods as the Indian system was found to be meeting the qualifying criteria under the carbon border adjustment mechanism.The decision will come as a gain for govt, which was trying to include carbon tax in the trade negotiations but the UK authorities did not agree to the proposal at that time. Besides, armed with the exemption, govt will make a fresh bid for a similar dispensation in the European Union where a trade deal has been finalized and is expected to be operationalized next year.While the indicative list is being released by the UK treasury in individual cases there may be issues that will need to be sorted out. Officials said that relief that can be claimed by an exporter will depend on the effective carbon price that the product faces and the entity will need to explain to authorities in the UK the extent of levy that has been paid.CBAM is a carbon pricing tool on imported goods designed to equalize carbon costs and prevent carbon leakage. While companies in the UK and EU face the tax, the mechanism is meant to ensure level-playing field. However, if a company bears a carbon pricing burden in the home market, it has to be factored in by authorities in the UK and EU, businesses have argued.
Article Summary: The UK has agreed to recognize India’s carbon credit trading scheme. The move will enable exporters to avoid “double taxation” The UK treasury has decided to exempt goods as the Indian system was found to be meeting qualifying criteria under carbon border adjustment mechanism.

Article Title: IIT Mandi Director recruitment 2026: Education Ministry invites applications, ₹2.25 lakh monthly salary on offer; check eligibility and deadline
Article Text:
The Ministry of Education has launched the process to appoint IIT Mandi’s next Director, with eligible senior academicians and administrators required to submit their applications by October 31, 2026. (ANI Video Grab)

Search-cum-Selection Committee to recommend candidates

Who can apply for the post?

₹2.25 lakh monthly salary for selected Director

Applicants must submit vision statement and justification

How to apply for IIT Mandi Director post

Appointment process begins ahead of change in IIT Mandi leadership

The Ministry of Education has initiated the process to appoint a new Director for the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Mandi, inviting applications from accomplished academicians and administrators with a strong record in teaching, research, and institutional leadership.The appointment process comes ahead of the end of the tenure of IIT Mandi's current Director, Laxmidhar Behera, whose term is scheduled to conclude in December 2026. The selected candidate will head one of India's premier technical institutions and will be appointed on a contractual basis for a period of five years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever comes earlier.According to the official notice issued by the Ministry of Education, IIT Mandi is an autonomous institution fully funded by the Government of India through the Ministry of Education.The appointment of the Director will be made after approval from the Competent Authority, based on recommendations of the Search-cum-Selection Committee. The committee will consider applications submitted in response to the advertisement as well as nominations received from eminent individuals.The recruitment process has opened an important opportunity for senior academicians and institutional leaders with experience in higher education and technical research to take charge of the Himalayan institute.The Ministry has laid down stringent eligibility conditions for candidates aspiring to lead IIT Mandi.Applicants are expected to possess a PhD with a first-class or equivalent qualification in the preceding degree, preferably in an Engineering discipline. However, the Ministry has indicated that candidates from Science, Mathematics and Management backgrounds may also be considered in exceptional cases.Candidates must also have an outstanding academic record throughout their career. They should have at least 10 years of teaching experience as a Professor at a reputed Engineering or Technology Institute or University and must have experience guiding PhD scholars.Apart from academic credentials, the Ministry has placed considerable emphasis on administrative experience and leadership. Applicants are expected to have at least five years of administrative experience along with demonstrated leadership capabilities.The applicant should preferably be below 60 years of age on the last date for submission of applications.The candidate selected for the top position at IIT Mandi will receive a revised monthly salary of ₹2,25,000, in addition to allowances admissible under government rules.The Director's role will involve providing academic and administrative leadership to the institution while steering its research, innovation, industry collaboration and long-term institutional development.Applicants will also be expected to demonstrate their understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing higher technical education.The Ministry has asked interested candidates to submit a detailed application in the prescribed format along with several supporting documents.Applicants must clearly outline their achievements in research, teaching, industry-academia collaborations and administration. They must also submit a two-page justification supporting their candidature and a separate two-page vision statement outlining their plans for the institution.In addition, candidates must provide the contact details of at least two distinguished individuals who are well acquainted with their professional work.The application, typed in the prescribed format along with the required enclosures, must be sent through Registered Post or Speed Post to the Ministry of Education.The application should be addressed to:The Under Secretary (TS.1)Department of Higher EducationMinistry of EducationH-01, Work Hall No. 21108, First FloorKartavya Bhawan - 2New Delhi – 110001Applications must reach the Ministry on or before October 31, 2026.Candidates currently employed in government departments, autonomous organisations or public sector undertakings are required to submit their applications through the proper channel. They may also send an advance copy to the Ministry.The envelope containing the application must carry the words “APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF DIRECTOR, IIT MANDI” prominently in bold.Applicants are also required to send one electronic copy of the application, preferably in MS Word format, to the email address specified by the Ministry.The notification sets in motion the process of selecting the next academic leader of IIT Mandi months before the completion of the incumbent Director's tenure in December.The advertisement was issued before controversy surrounding an inappropriate poster involving the institution emerged. The Ministry's recruitment process, however, is focused on identifying a candidate with a distinguished academic background, proven administrative experience and the ability to provide strategic leadership to one of the country's leading IITs.With the October 31 deadline now in place, the search for IIT Mandi's next Director has formally begun, with the Ministry looking for an academic leader capable of shaping the institution's next phase of growth and strengthening its position in India's expanding higher education and research ecosystem.
Article Summary: The Ministry of Education has launched the process to appoint IIT Mandi’s next Director, with eligible senior academicians and administrators required to submit their applications by October 31, 2026. The selected candidate will head one of India's premier technical institutions and will be appointed on a contractual basis for a period of five years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever comes earlier. The appointment process comes ahead of the end of the tenure of the current Director, Laxmidhar Behera.
